summary: Iteration 10 backend-only retest of the share unlock client-IP derivation (xff[-TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS], with hops=3). Share suites: 31/32 passed. Full regression: 98 passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped. WORKING: (a) Via the public URL, guest A rotating spoofed X-Forwarded-For values made of valid IPs (single, 2-entry, 3-entry, none) gets 401 five times, then 429, including for the correct password. (b) A different real client (internal port 8001, 3rd-from-right hop differs) is NOT locked out by A: correct password gives 200 and a wrong one gives 401. The key A got from the public request equals the pod egress IP at xff[-3], so a crafted chain with that IP gets 429. (c) On the internal port, changing left-most or Cloudflare-hop entries does not bypass. Client B's success resets B's own counter, and B is then limited to 5 again. (d) The per-token cap holds: 20 failures across 4 IPs, then 429 for a new IP, for the correct password, and on the public path. (e) bcrypt now runs in a thread, and correct/wrong/changed passwords behave as before. (f) Regression of enable/400 without password/422 short password/client 403/unpublished 404/meta/no leak/unlock+view/forged JWT/password change invalidates/disable revokes after re-enable/regenerate/DB bcrypt hash all passed. NEW HIGH FINDING: if the client sends a malformed (non-IP) X-Forwarded-For value such as 'x' or 'a, b, c, d', the Google LB appends an extra hop (35.191.x.x). The chain becomes '<spoof>,<real client>,<CF egress>,34.8.246.104, 35.191.x.x', so xff[-3] is the Cloudflare egress IP, which rotates per request. One machine then gets 20 wrong attempts instead of 5 and reaches the per-token cap. That locks out ALL guests of the link for 15 min: confirmed, 20x 401, then 429 for an unrelated guest using the correct password.

critical.issue: Per-IP limit bypass and single-machine lockout DoS via a malformed client XFF. Captured chains (temporary debug log, since removed): valid client XFF '1.2.3.4' -> '1.2.3.4,136.70.105.25,104.22.104.98,34.8.246.104' (len ok, xff[-3]=real client). Malformed client XFF 'x' -> 'x,136.70.105.25,172.71.194.137,34.8.246.104, 35.191.126.58': the Google GFE appends a 35.191.0.0/16 hop, so xff[-3]=172.71.194.137 (Cloudflare egress, varies per request). Reproduced deterministically 3 times. Effect: 20 wrong guesses from one IP, then the per-token cap (20) locks out every legitimate guest for 15 min, and this can repeat every 15 min. Brute force stays bounded at 20 per 15 min per token. Fix: do not use a fixed index. Walk the XFF from the right, skip entries in trusted proxy ranges (Google LB/GFE 35.191.0.0/16, 130.211.0.0/22, 34.8.246.104 or a configurable TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS, plus the Cloudflare published IPv4/IPv6 ranges), and take the first untrusted, valid ipaddress.ip_address() entry. Fall back to client.host. Alternatively strip trailing 35.191.x/130.211.x hops before applying xff[-2] (the hop added by the CF worker).

minor.issue: When len(xff) < hops it falls back to xff[0], which is client-controlled. That is harmless here because public chains are always >=3 long, but if production ingress has fewer hops (e.g. 2), a client-supplied first entry becomes the key, which is fully spoofable. Prefer the right-most-untrusted approach above, or fall back to xff[-1]/client.host instead of xff[0].
Still in-memory and per-worker; it resets on restart (unchanged, known).

action_items: HIGH: make client-IP derivation robust to a variable number of trailing proxy hops: skip trusted proxy CIDRs from the right (Google 35.191.0.0/16, 130.211.0.0/22, the LB IP, Cloudflare ranges) and take the first valid untrusted IP. Today a malformed client XFF ('x') shifts the chain, so xff[-3] becomes a rotating Cloudflare egress IP. One machine then gets 20 tries and locks out all guests through the per-token cap. Test: tests/test_share_ratelimit.py::TestPublicMalformedXffBypass must pass.
LOW: avoid the xff[0] fallback for short chains (client-controlled).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py share_unlock: ip = xff[-hops] assumes a fixed number of appended hops. The Google LB appends an extra 35.191.x hop when the incoming XFF is malformed, so the index is attacker-influenced.
share_unlock: entries are not validated as IPs (ipaddress), so junk values pass through as keys.
bcrypt hashpw/checkpw now run in asyncio.to_thread: OK.
set_share: version bump only on enabled true->false and on password change: OK (verified again).
